chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Divorce is that a man says to his wife, ‘Choose.’ If she chooses herself, then she has separated from him, and he is [only] a suitor among the suitors. But if she chooses her husband, then it is nothing. Or he says, ‘You are divorced.’ Whichever of these he does, she becomes forbidden to him. And there is no divorce, no khulʿ, no mubārāʾah, and no takhyīr except in a state of purity, without intercourse, and with the testimony of two witnesses.

key_terms.تَخْيِيرٌ: granting the wife the choice regarding continuation of marriage
key_terms.خُلْعٌ: a form of separation initiated through compensation from the wife
key_terms.طَالِقٌ: divorced; the explicit formula of divorce
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: a state of ritual purity from menstruation in this legal context
key_terms.ٱخْتَارِي: choose for yourself; a formula of giving the wife the option
key_terms.ٱلطَّلَاقُ: divorce as a legal dissolution of marriage

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce, khulʿ, or takhyīr in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning divorce and the form of giving a wife the choice regarding separation. It also establishes that divorce, khulʿ, mubārāʾah, and takhyīr are only valid when performed in a state of purity without intercourse and in the presence of two witnesses.
